title: Gearshift External Controls — 3160 Manual
introduction: For the 6-Speed Manual Transmission – 3160, this overview identifies the external shift controls and explains how the driver’s movement reaches the transmission. I picture the lever as a mechanical messenger: moving it sends the selection through a lever attached to the gearbox. This is a component and operation guide, without removal, adjustment or fault-testing instructions.

edits.text: The manual transmission’s external controls include the following components:
edits.why: These names identify the external control parts discussed here; they are not an inventory of the transmission’s internal gear-selection components.

edits.text: Gearshift lever assembly: the driver-operated shift control.
Gearshift lever knob: the part the driver grips.
Gearshift lever boot: the covering around the lever.
How Shift Movement Reaches the Transmission
The driver controls the manual transmission with a floor-mounted gearshift lever in the floor console. Moving that gearshift lever transmits movement through a lever attached to the transmission.
edits.why: This describes the mechanical path of the driver’s shift input. It does not establish an adjustment method or determine why a particular shift feels difficult.
